newsitem.title: SPAIN: Multiplier rise to boost Spain Ibex futures trade. [CORRECTED 18:22 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Multiplier rise to boost Spain Ibex futures trade. [CORRECTED 18:22 GMT]

text.p: A increase in the value of Spanish stock market futures contracts is likely to boost traded volume by making it easier for institutions to operate on the MEFF futures exchange, market sources said on Wednesday.
Earlier today MEFF annnounced an increase in the multiplier on Ibex-35 futures contracts to 1,000 from the current 100.

Up to now the nominal on the contracts was 100 times the value of the Ibex, for instance 430,000 pesetas with the Ibex at 4,300, while for the new contract the nominal will be 1,000 times the value of the Ibex which is 4.3 million (corrects from 64.3 million) in the above example.

"From the point of view of institutional investors the measure is quite good, because from now on they will need to trade far fewer contracts for the same nominal," said Miguel Cuenca, head of derivatives trading at Credit Lyonnais Securities in Madrid.
"With the new contract, institutions reduce their internal settlement expenses which are normally calculated per contract and not per nominal."
Traders agreed that the measure would probably boost trading volume in the future.

"The measure won't discriminate against individual clients, they will simply trade two contracts instead of 20 and for institutions it will be more profitable, so it would be normal for it to produce a rise in trade," said Cuenca.
Some traders believe the current size of the contract, which is relatively low compared to other markets, has complicated the entry of some foreign clients into the Spanish market.

"If the measure is adopted it is because there is a belief it will increase volume," said a trader at Benito y Monjardin. "There are in fact people who are going into other markets and not here because of the size of the contract."

"It could be that in the short term we won't see an signficant rise in volume, but there is a precedent, the Mibor Plus, which increased its multiplier by 10 and the rise in volume has been considerable," he added.
The market had been awaiting such a decision by MEFF for months.
"We were expecting an increase in the multiplier in the terms finally decided for months," said a trader. "Market conditions demanded it."
